newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swap - Regrade narrows on arb fears.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swap - Regrade narrows on arb fears.

text.p: Singapore jet fuel swaps eased late afternoon on Tuesday on fears of fresh arbitrage shipments from the Mediterranean and incremental supplies as regional refiners optimise jet production, traders said.
"The regrade is under pressure because some people think it might be over done," one trader said.
July regrade was last quoted at $1.85/$2.00 per barrel down from Monday's $2.00/$2.20, brokers said.
Traders said further evidence for the top-heavy prompt market could also be seen from the forward regrades quotes where both August and September are valued below July.
August and September were quoted at $1.55/$1/75, down about 25 cents from Monday and about 30 cents more than July.
Traders said it was unusual for the late third quarter months to be valued under the front months as demand is higher in the later months as winter demand kicks in.
"I think July is over valued at the moment becuase of the prompt physical buying interest," said a trader.
Traders said July is likely to come under selling pressure over the next few days as the arbitrage players look to offload their cargoes in the local spot physical market.
In addition to the arbitrage cargoes, regional refiners who have raised jet production also have surplus cargoes to sell.
Physical jet fuel was last offered at $24.65 per barrel free-on-board on talks that a cargo traded late last week at $24.50, traders said.
Gas oil swaps is steady despite claims that the market is oversupplied as seen by the high stock level and the absence of fresh Chinese demand despite the long wait.

July swaps were indicated at $22.50/$22.65 per barrel, almost unchanged from Monday. August was quoted at $22.95/$23.10, up five to 10 cents from Monday in a steep contango market with September quoted at $23.45/$23.60.
Fuel oil remained steady despite physical selling pressure on Monday also partly due to the firmer crude, brokers said.
July swaps was quoted at $98.50/$99.00 per tonne, and August at $98.00/$98.50. July traded earlier in the day at $98.90 and August at $98.25, they said.
